data.name: Zenethics Lab : Outbreak
data.detailed_description:
You wake up in the middle of the night and your girlfriend isn't by your side. In fact she hasn't responded to your messages since she left for work in the morning. You are worried and decide to go look for her at the lab she's working.

Gameplay


  • A mix of hack'n slash and third person shooter
  • View frop top of the scene
  • Die and retry : each game will provide you points that you can use to empower you and allow you to go further in the next try
  • Endless mode : once you finish most of the story you will unlock endless mode where you will encounter empowered enemies in random generated levels
  • Race mode : once you finish most of tyhe story you will unlock race mode were you will have to complete levels from the campain and specials ones as fast as you can

Features


  • Story mode of 40 levels + 6 shortcuts
  • Random generated levels after level 15
  • Specific levels for Endless and Race modes
  • Choose between 60 perks including 20 weapons to unlock
  • 13 types of monsters including 4 bosses
  • Combo system and adrenaline bar
  • Light/shadow mechanics allowing deeper immersion in the game
  • Full controller support
  • Steamcloud

content_descriptors.notes: The game plunges you into a dark and horrifying atmosphere, where you must fight monsters to progress. Combat is violent and bloody, and death is an integral part of the gameplay, following a classic die-and-retry approach. The game features graphic violence.

reviews.review:
Zenethics Lab: Outbreak is an independent action-adventure game that combines intense combat, horror atmosphere, and RPG-inspired progression into a challenging experience built around survival and repeated attempts. Developed and published by Gilles Schaeck, the game blends hack-and-slash mechanics with shooting elements while incorporating permanent upgrades that reward persistence. Its top-down perspective, violent encounters, and mysterious laboratory setting establish an interesting foundation for players who appreciate action games with roguelite characteristics.

The story begins when the protagonist awakens during the night and discovers that his girlfriend has mysteriously disappeared. Having received no response to his messages since she departed for work, he decides to investigate the laboratory where she is employed. What initially appears to be a straightforward search quickly develops into a dangerous confrontation with horrifying creatures. Although the narrative premise is relatively simple, it provides sufficient motivation for exploring the facility and surviving its numerous threats. The emphasis remains firmly on gameplay rather than elaborate storytelling, making the experience particularly suitable for players who prioritize combat and progression.

The combat system combines close-range fighting with shooting mechanics, creating opportunities for different offensive approaches. The overhead camera provides a broad view of surrounding environments, allowing players to monitor approaching enemies and adjust their positioning. A combo system and adrenaline bar introduce additional mechanics intended to reward aggressive and effective fighting. These features give encounters more tactical potential, although their overall effectiveness depends on the responsiveness of the controls and the variety of enemy behaviors.

One of the game's strongest concepts is its progression system, which transforms defeat into an opportunity for improvement. Players accumulate points during their attempts and use them to strengthen their character before returning to the action. This approach encourages experimentation and reduces the frustration of repeatedly encountering difficult sections. Rather than requiring flawless performance immediately, the game allows gradual advancement through improved abilities and equipment. However, players who dislike repetitive gameplay may find this structure less appealing, particularly when progress requires multiple unsuccessful attempts.

Character customization offers considerable potential through 60 available perks, including 20 unlockable weapons. These options provide opportunities to improve combat effectiveness and experiment with different approaches to surviving encounters. The selection of weapons is especially appealing because it introduces variety into repeated attempts. Nevertheless, the true value of these upgrades depends on whether they meaningfully influence gameplay rather than simply providing incremental statistical improvements.

The campaign features 40 levels and six shortcuts, offering a substantial progression structure for a modest independent production. Shortcuts are particularly useful in a game emphasizing repeated attempts because they can reduce unnecessary repetition and make difficult areas more accessible. Procedurally generated environments appear after the fifteenth level, introducing unpredictability into later stages. This design encourages adaptability and improves replayability, although randomly generated layouts may occasionally lack the deliberate pacing of handcrafted environments.

Enemy encounters involve 13 monster types, including four bosses. These creatures provide the primary obstacles throughout the adventure, while boss battles introduce opportunities for more demanding confrontations. Although the enemy roster is relatively limited compared with the campaign's length, different enemy combinations and increasing difficulty can help maintain engagement. The game's dark atmosphere is reinforced by lighting and shadow mechanics that contribute to its unsettling laboratory environments. Graphic violence, bloody encounters, and frequent deaths further establish its identity as a horror-themed action experience.

Additional gameplay modes extend the experience beyond the main campaign. Endless Mode becomes available after substantial story progression and challenges players with strengthened enemies across randomly generated environments. Race Mode introduces a different objective by encouraging players to complete campaign stages and specially designed levels as quickly as possible. Together, these modes provide additional reasons to revisit the game, improve combat efficiency, and experiment with different character builds.

The inclusion of Steam achievements, cloud saving, and leaderboards adds practical value to the overall package. Achievements encourage additional objectives, while leaderboards complement the competitive nature of speed-focused challenges. The game also features English and French interface and subtitle support. Its modest system requirements, including 1 GB of RAM and approximately 300 MB of storage, make it relatively accessible to players using less powerful computers.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game does not have a confirmed official Verified or Playable classification. However, its full controller support, top-down presentation, and lightweight hardware requirements are encouraging characteristics for handheld gaming. Since Windows is the listed supported operating system, Steam Deck users would likely need Proton compatibility. Actual performance, stability, and control functionality remain unconfirmed, so compatibility should be considered unverified rather than guaranteed.

The game's principal weaknesses concern its potentially repetitive progression, limited enemy variety, and relatively straightforward narrative. Its combat systems and upgrade selection are promising, but the overall experience depends heavily on their execution and balance. Players expecting cinematic storytelling or extensive environmental exploration may find its action-focused structure somewhat restrictive. Nevertheless, those who enjoy challenging encounters, permanent improvements, and replayable gameplay modes may appreciate its approach.

Overall, Zenethics Lab: Outbreak presents an interesting combination of laboratory horror, fast-paced action, and progression-driven gameplay. Its extensive upgrade selection, multiple gameplay modes, and procedural environments provide a solid foundation for replayability, even if its modest production scope and potential repetition limit its broader appeal. It is particularly worth considering for players who enjoy smaller independent action games built around persistence and character development.

A promising horror-themed action experience with rewarding progression concepts and worthwhile replayability features, although its limited enemy variety and repetitive structure may prevent it from achieving its full potential. 

Rating: 6/10
